records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Ww A patient complains of diplopia on reading or walking downstairs, which of the following cranial nerves is most likely to be affected: & Trochlear nerve 70%
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve 2%
records.explanation: Trochlear nerve palsy causes weakness of downward gaze. The patient complains of difficulty reading or walking downstairs and of vertical diplopia. The eye is extorted and may be elevated and the patient may head tilt to the opposite side of the palsy to compensate. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: A 64 year old lady complains of a sore right eye. On examination, you note a normal corneal blink reflex on her left side but no consensual blink reflex on her right side. A lesion in which of the following structures is most likely to cause this clinical picture:
records.explanation: The corneal blink reflex is an involuntary blinking of the eyelids, mediated by the orbicularis oculi muscle, and elicited by stimulation of the cornea. The afferent pathway is the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve, and the efferent pathway is the facial nerve. Loss of the consensual corneal blink reflex suggests loss of the efferent pathway on this side. ls > Vv
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Oculomotor (CN Ill) palsy with sparing of the pupillary reflex is most likely caused by which of the following:
options: Aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery
records.explanation: Compressive causes of CN III palsy cause early pupillary dilatation because the parasympathetic fibres run peripherally in the nerve and are easily compressed. In diabetes mellitus the lesions are ischaemic rather than compressive and therefore typically affect the central fibres resulting in pupillary sparing. Vv
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Which of the following clinical features would you most expect to see in a glossopharyngeal nerve palsy:
options: Loss of jaw jerk 2% Loss of gag reflex 81%
records.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve is the afferent pathway of the gag reflex. Tongue weakness and fasciculations may be seen in hypoglossal nerve palsy. Loss of jaw jerk may be seen in palsy of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. Hoarseness and uvular deviation may been seen in vagus nerve palsy. Vv
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: we Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the gag reflex:
records.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve is the afferent pathway of the gag reflex. The vagus nerve is the efferent pathway of the gag reflex. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Ww A patient complains of headaches and dizziness. Imaging reveals a tumour at the cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following nerves will most likely be affected by this tumour:
records.explanation: The vestibulocochlear nerve and facial nerve both emerge from the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle so are the nerves most likely to be affected by a tumour in this location. Vv
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Regarding the abducens nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The abducens nerve innervates the inferior oblique muscle. (<7 Abducens nerve palsy results in a vertical diplopia. 4%
The abducens nerve originates in the medulla.
The abducens nerve enters the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure.
Abducens nerve palsy results in a convergent squint.
records.explanation: The abducens nerve originates in the pons and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure to innervate the lateral rectus muscle. Abducens nerve palsy results in a convergent squint and horizontal diplopia. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: A patient complains of diplopia and on examination is found to have a depressed and abducted eye with ptosis. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
records.explanation: Oculomotor (CN III) nerve palsy results in a depressed and abducted (down and out) eye, diplopia, ptosis and a fixed and dilated pupil. Vv
